manifest.name: dsh-roles-zeta
manifest.description: Role-based subagent delegation for DeepSeek Harness: one delegate tool over a folder of role files, with a roster that ships and stays overridable

scripts.check: node --check lib/index.js && node --check lib/client.js && npm pack --dry-run

bundle.text:
# The dsh-roles-zeta bundle patch: one host-plane row that registers the
# `delegate` tool over the host `ctx.subagents` seam.
#
# Host plane on purpose: the subagent registry and its spawn/fork providers are
# process singletons mounted by `dsh-base` at the profile root, so this row
# resolves the same instance every preset already uses. A row here is visible to
# every agent in every preset, including `standard`, without copying a preset.
#
# Nothing in this file names a machine path. The role directory defaults to
# `<dshHome>/agents` (`$DSH_HOME`, else `~/.dsh`); set `rolesDir` only to keep
# roles somewhere else, and set `dshHome` only to read them from a harness home
# other than the one this process resolved.
#
# Nothing here names a model either. A role names its own route — a bare model id
# such as `deepseek-flash`, or an exact `provider/model` — and the plugin resolves
# it against this Session's `subagent-model-selection` allowed routes first and
# the registered provider catalogs second. Tick the models you want in the DSH
# settings and the roles follow; switch machines and nothing in this file changes.
#
# `routes` is therefore optional and empty by default. Add an alias only when you
# want indirection, so a role can say `deep` and this file decides what `deep`
# means on this machine:
#
#   routes:
#     deep: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-flash }
#
# Three optional surfaces mount only where their host service exists and need no
# configuration: one `/<id>` slash command per role (`commands`, `commandPrefix`),
# the Settings → Role agents page over a few JSON routes (`settingsPage`), and a
# watcher on the role directory (`watchRolesDir`). Set any of them to `false`
# here to leave it out.
#
# `modelSelectionSettings` is deliberately absent. A standing composition with it
# requires both a scoped preset Context and it would collide with the `subagent`
# row that already owns the global `list_subagent_models` name. The tool reaches
# the same setting through `ctx.get('subagentModelSelection')` instead: when a
# Session has one enabled, `provider` and `model` become per-call parameters
# validated against it.

- insert:
    - id: roles-zeta
      # The row names this package by its own package name, the same way a
      # bundle patch normally does. A fork republished under another name must
      # update this line to match.
      name: dsh-roles-zeta
      config:
        provider: spawn
        toolName: delegate
        backgroundMode: continuable
        maxDepth: 2

readme.text: English | [繁體中文](README.zh-TW.md) | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

`dsh-roles-zeta` gives a dsh agent one `delegate` tool and a folder of role
files. A call names a role; the role file supplies the child's persona, model
route, reasoning effort, and tool surface. It sits on the same `ctx.subagents`
service the built-in `subagent` tool uses, so providers, delegation depth,
continuation, and background settlement keep working unchanged. The built-in
`subagent` and `subagent_fork` tools stay mounted: they let the model pick a
route per call, while a role is fixed when the file is written.

Each role reaches its child as an Agent Preset: a copy of the calling agent's
own preset with the role's persona and only the plugins its tools need (see
[Roles as agent presets](#roles-as-agent-presets)). This needs dsh 0.2.1-rc.2
or later, where a delegation carries no persona or tool filter of its own.

Around the tool sit three surfaces, each mounted only where its host service
exists: one slash command per role in the Web input box, a **Role agents**
page in the Web settings, and a watcher on the role directory so an edit
reaches the next call without recomposing the profile.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-roles-zeta

```

Profiles are separate install roots, so install into each profile that should
have it. `github:zeta987/dsh-roles-zeta` and `file:<path>` specs work too. On
the first load the eight role files are written to `$DSH_HOME/agents`
~/.dsh/agents
├── code-mapper-lite.md   explorer.md            log-distiller.md   triage.md
├── deep-coordinator.md   hypothesis-debate.md   reviewer.md        worker.md
└── .seeded.json
```

Nothing updates on its own: `dsh plugin` forwards to pnpm inside the profile,
starting the host installs nothing, and no page checks a registry. To move to
a release:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-roles-zeta@0.4.0

```

Name the version. `update` stays inside the `^0.x` range pnpm wrote at install
time, and pnpm 11+ hides a version published less than 24 hours ago from
`outdated` and `@latest` (`minimumReleaseAge`); an explicit version installs
right away. Role files you edited are left alone; shipped ones you never
touched are refreshed on the next load.

Every loaded role is a command in the Web input box. Type `/` to see them next
to `/plan` and `/goal`; `/reviewer look at lib/index.js` queues a turn asking
the agent to call `delegate` with role `reviewer` and that text as the task,
run it in the foreground, and relay the result. The delegation therefore stays
in the transcript as an ordinary tool call, where `/plan <message>` puts its
message too.

Commands follow the roster: adding, renaming, or removing a role re-registers
them and the menu refreshes. A role whose id collides with another plugin's
command is skipped as a command (logged) and still works through the tool.
`commands: false` mounts none; `commandPrefix: "r-"` gives `/r-reviewer`.

Settings → **Role agents** lists the roster with a badge per role (shipped,
yours, edited) and edits one role at a time: id, the `when` line, the route
(with the session's allowed routes as suggestions), the effort, the tools as a
checklist of what is registered right now (or "inherit everything" plus the
delegation toggle), and the persona. Saving writes `<id>.md` into
`$DSH_HOME/agents`, the same file you would write by hand.

| Button | On disk |
|---|---|
| Delete, on a role you added | Removes the file |
| Delete, on a shipped role | Leaves a `disabled: true` stub so the packaged copy stops loading; listed under *Disabled shipped roles* until restored |
| Restore this role | Copies the shipped file back over yours |
| Restore the shipped roles | The same for all eight; roles you added are never touched |

The page is a browser module over JSON routes under `/__dsh/roles-zeta/`,
gated by the same browser-session cookie and Host/Origin fence as the rest of
the Web API. `settingsPage: false` mounts neither.

One Markdown file per role: frontmatter for the machine fields, body as the
child's persona prefix.

```markdown
---
id: reviewer
when: Deep read-only reviewer for correctness, regressions, edge cases, and missing tests.
route: deepseek-official/deepseek-flash

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | Role id; the `_` spelling resolves to the same role |
| `when` | yes | One line; the model's menu entry and the command description |
| `route` | no | A model id (`deepseek-flash`) or an exact `provider/model` |
| `effort` | no | `off`/`minimal`/`low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max`, clamped per route |
| `allow` | no | Tool names the child needs; the plugins that register them are kept (per plugin, see below) and the child is then masked to exactly these names; omitted inherits everything, `[]` keeps no tool plugin |
| `delegation` | no | `true` keeps the delegation plugins in a child without an `allow` list |
| `disabled` | no | `true` removes a shipped role |

A role with an `allow` list can delegate only if the list names the delegation
tools; one without an `allow` list only with `delegation: true`.

Two roots, later winning: the package's own `roles/*.md`, then
`$DSH_HOME/agents`. The package seeds its roster into your directory on first
load and keeps it managed while you leave it alone:

| What you do | Next load |
|---|---|
| Nothing | Shipped files follow the package; a release that changes a role updates it |
| Edit one | It is yours and is never overwritten again |
| Delete one | It is not seeded again, but the packaged copy still loads; remove the role itself with a `disabled` stub or the settings page |
| Add one | It loads alongside the shipped roles |

`.seeded.json` records what the package wrote. A file you drop in replaces the
shipped role by id; a stub with only `id` and `disabled: true` removes it. The
directory is watched, so any change is re-read after a short quiet period.
`seedRolesDir: false` stops the package from writing into your directory;
`watchRolesDir: false` reads it once per composition.

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: roles-zeta
      name: dsh-roles-zeta
      config:

No model and no path appears here: role files name their route and the plugin
resolves it. The row is host plane, so every agent in every preset sees the
tool.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `dshHome` | `$DSH_HOME`, else `~/.dsh` | Harness home the role directory is derived from |
| `rolesDir` | `$DSH_HOME/agents` | Your role directory: seed target and override root |
| `seedRolesDir` | `true` | Write the shipped roster into `rolesDir` and keep it current while unedited |
| `watchRolesDir` | `true` | Reload the roster when a file in `rolesDir` changes |
| `commands` | `true` | One `/<id>` slash command per role |
| `commandPrefix` | (empty) | Text placed before every command name |
| `settingsPage` | `true` | Mount the settings API and page |
| `provider` | `spawn` | `ctx.subagents` provider name |
| `toolName` | `delegate` | Model-facing tool name |
| `backgroundMode` | `continuable` | `continuable` returns a durable child id; `one-shot` a job id |
| `enableRunInBackground` | `true` | Expose `run_in_background` |
| `maxDepth` | `2` | Delegation-depth cap for a started child |
| `defaultRoute` | (empty) | Used when a role names no `route:` |
| `routes` | `{}` | Alias table: `deep: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-flash }` lets roles say `route: deep` |

A `route:` is looked up in this order: the row's `routes` aliases; the
session's `subagent-model-selection` allowed list (the models ticked in the
DSH settings); the registered providers' catalogs; an inline
`model: { provider, model }` on the role. The catalog step is what lets a
headless profile resolve without any settings surface. When the allowed list
is enabled it also gates the role's route: a registered model the list
excludes is rejected with a message, not run quietly.

With no route named anywhere the child inherits the calling agent's provider
and model, and the result says so; the plugin never picks from the allowed
list by itself. A bare model id registered under two providers must be written
as `provider/model`.

Effort is clamped onto the levels the route advertises, the higher one on a
tie: `deepseek-flash` offers `off`/`low`/`high`/`max`, so `medium` becomes
`high` and `xhigh` becomes `max`. The shipped roles all say `high`. A
substitution is reported in the delegation result.

A delegation request names an Agent Preset for the child to mount, and that
preset alone decides the child's persona and tools. On its first call for a
role, the plugin registers one preset for that role and the caller's preset:

- **Id** `roles-zeta/<role>@<parent preset>`, for example
  `roles-zeta/reviewer@standard`, named `Role: reviewer (standard)`.
- **Rows** are the parent preset's own plugin rows, copied. The
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona` row's `prefix` becomes the role body; its suffix
  and other settings stay. A parent without a persona row gets one.
- **Tool plugins** are filtered by plugin row, not by tool. dsh does not
  record which plugin registered a tool, so the plugin carries a table of the
  shipped tool plugins and the names each one registers (`dsh-tool-fs`:
  `read`, `write`, `edit`, `read_image`; `dsh-tool-fs-search`: `glob`,
  `grep`; and so on). With an `allow` list, a tool plugin stays when it
  registers at least one allowed name. Without one, every plugin stays except
  those registering a delegation tool (`subagent`, `subagent_fork`, `workflow`,
  `ralph`), unless `delegation: true`. `allow: []` keeps no tool plugin.
- **Rows the table does not know** (third-party plugins, infrastructure such
  as `dsh-skill-filesystem` or compaction) are kept as they are, because
  another row may depend on them. A group that loses every row is dropped.
- **A per-tool mask** is then applied to

The preset is reused while the role file and the parent preset stay the same;
editing either registers a fresh one on the next call. A role child that
delegates again clones the original parent preset, so personas never stack.
The log says which rows each role preset left out.

One tool schema per session: a roster line per role and the allowed routes in
the description; parameters `role`, `description`, `prompt`, an optional
`route` alias, `provider`/`model` when the session enables model selection,
and `run_in_background`. A call resolves the role, preflights the route,
registers or reuses the role's preset, and starts one child on it. A
foreground call returns the child's final text; a continuable background call
returns `started subagent <id>` and settles through the runtime's notice.

- **The preset still loads whole plugins; the mask hides the extras.** A kept
  `dsh-tool-fs` row still mounts `write`, `edit`, and `read_image` for a
  reviewer allowed `read`, and host-plane tools (`delegate`,
  `working_directory`, the MCP resource tools, every connected MCP server's
  `mcp__*` tools) still exist outside the preset. Neither reaches the child:
  the per-tool mask hides every name its `allow` list does not give, and a
  role without one loses `delegate` and the delegation tools unless
  `delegation: true`. The mask is computed when the child is created, so an
  allowed tool that registers later (an MCP server that connects afterwards)
  stays hidden from that child, and a tool the child registers in its own
  scope (its structured-output tool) is never masked.
- **Role presets show up next to the shipped ones.** They are ordinary Agent
  Presets, so the Web preset picker lists them after `standard`, `cordis`,
  and the rest.
- **Resuming a background child after a restart needs its preset again.**
  Role presets are registered on first use. Messaging a role child that was
  started before the host restarted fails with an unknown-preset error until

`dsh-roles-zeta` 为 dsh agent 提供一个 `delegate` 工具和一个角色文件文件夹。调用时指定角色，角色文件提供该 child 的 persona、模型路线、reasoning effort 与工具范围。它架在内置 `subagent` 工具所用的同一个 `ctx.subagents` 服务上，所以 provider、委派深度、续谈与后台结算全部照旧。内置的 `subagent` 与 `subagent_fork` 继续挂着：它们让模型每次调用自己挑路线，而角色是写文件时就固定的。

每个角色以 Agent Preset 的形式交给 child：复制调用者自己的 preset，换上角色的 persona，只保留角色工具需要的插件（见[角色即 agent preset](#角色即-agent-preset)）。需要 dsh 0.2.1-rc.2 以上；从这版起，委派请求本身不再带 persona 或工具过滤器。
工具旁边有三个界面，各自只在对应的 host 服务存在时挂载：Web 输入框里每个角色一条斜杠指令、Web 设置里的“角色代理”页，以及角色目录的监控，改动不必重新组合 profile 就会进到下一次调用。

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-roles-zeta

```

profile 是各自独立的安装根，要用的每个 profile 都装一次。`github:zeta987/dsh-roles-zeta` 与 `file:<path>` 也可以。第一次加载时八个角色文件会写进 `$DSH_HOME/agents`（`$DSH_HOME` 默认 `~/.dsh`），新 session 就有一个 `delegate` 工具，描述里列出它们。

```
~/.dsh/agents
├── code-mapper-lite.md   explorer.md            log-distiller.md   triage.md
├── deep-coordinator.md   hypothesis-debate.md   reviewer.md        worker.md
└── .seeded.json
```

不会自动更新：`dsh plugin` 是在 profile 目录里转发给 pnpm，启动 host 不会安装任何东西，也没有任何页面会查 registry。要换到某个版本：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-roles-zeta@0.4.0

```

版本要明确写出。`update` 只在安装时 pnpm 写下的 `^0.x` 范围内移动；pnpm 11 起会把发布未满 24 小时的版本从 `outdated` 与 `@latest` 里藏起来（`minimumReleaseAge`），明确指定版本则立刻能装。你改过的角色文件不会被动；没碰过的内置角色会在下次加载时刷新。

每个加载的角色都是 Web 输入框里的一条指令。输入 `/` 就会看到它们和 `/plan`、`/goal` 并列；`/reviewer look at lib/index.js` 会排进一轮对话，要求 agent 以 `reviewer` 角色调用 `delegate`、把这段文字当任务、在前台跑完并转述结果。所以委派会留在对话记录里，就是一次普通的工具调用，跟 `/plan <message>` 放消息的位置相同。

指令跟着角色列表走：新增、改名或移除角色都会重新注册，菜单自己更新。角色 id 撞到其他 plugin 的指令名时，该角色不注册成指令（log 会说明），但仍可通过工具使用。`commands: false` 就完全不挂；`commandPrefix: "r-"` 得到 `/r-reviewer`。

设置 → **角色代理** 列出角色列表，每个角色有标签（内置、自定义、已修改），一次编辑一个角色：id、`when` 说明、路线（session 允许的路线会列成建议）、推理强度、工具（当前已注册工具的勾选清单，或“沿用全部”加上委派开关）以及角色指示。保存会把 `<id>.md` 写进 `$DSH_HOME/agents`，跟你手写的是同一个文件。

| 按钮 | 对磁盘做的事 |
|---|---|
| 删除（自定义角色） | 移除文件 |
| 删除（内置角色） | 留下 `disabled: true` 停用文件，包内的副本不再加载；恢复前列在“已停用的内置角色” |
| 恢复此角色 | 把包内的文件复制回来覆盖你的版本 |
| 恢复内置角色 | 八个一起做；你自己新增的角色一律不动 |

这页是 `/__dsh/roles-zeta/` 底下几条 JSON 路由之上的浏览器模块，跟其他 Web API 一样受浏览器 session cookie 与 Host／Origin 信任检查把关。`settingsPage: false` 就两者都不挂。

一个角色一个 Markdown 文件：frontmatter 放机器字段，正文是 child 的 persona prefix。

```markdown
---
id: reviewer
when: Deep read-only reviewer for correctness, regressions, edge cases, and missing tests.
route: deepseek-official/deepseek-flash

| 字段 | 必填 | 语义 |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | 是 | 角色 id；下划线写法解析到同一个角色 |
| `when` | 是 | 一行；模型的菜单项，也是指令说明 |
| `route` | 否 | 模型 id（`deepseek-flash`）或完整的 `provider/model` |
| `effort` | 否 | `off`／`minimal`／`low`／`medium`／`high`／`xhigh`／`max`，按路线夹到可用层级 |
| `allow` | 否 | child 需要的工具名；注册这些工具的插件会被保留（以插件为单位，见下文），之后 child 会被遮罩成只剩这些名称；省略则继承全部，`[]` 不保留任何工具插件 |
| `delegation` | 否 | `true` 让没有 `allow` 的 child 保留委派插件 |
| `disabled` | 否 | `true` 移除一个内置角色 |
有 `allow` 的角色只有清单里列了委派工具才能委派；没有 `allow` 的只有 `delegation: true` 才能。

两层来源，后者覆盖前者：包自己的 `roles/*.md`，然后是 `$DSH_HOME/agents`。包第一次加载时把角色列表植入你的目录，你不碰它就一直由包管理：

| 你做了什么 | 下次加载 |
|---|---|
| 什么都不做 | 内置文件跟着包；新版本改了角色就更新 |
| 改了一个 | 它变成你的，不再被覆盖 |
| 删了一个 | 不会再植入，但包内的副本照样加载；要真正拿掉角色，用 `disabled` stub 或设置页 |
| 自己加一个 | 与内置角色一起加载 |

`.seeded.json` 记着包写了什么。你放进去的文件会按 id 取代内置角色；只有 `id` 与 `disabled: true` 的 stub 会移除它。目录是被监控的，任何变动在安静一小段时间后重新读取。`seedRolesDir: false` 让包不写入你的目录；`watchRolesDir: false` 改成每次组合只读一次。

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: roles-zeta
      name: dsh-roles-zeta
      config:

这里没有任何模型也没有任何路径：角色文件自己指名路线，插件负责解析。这条 row 在 host plane，所以每个 preset 的每个 agent 都能看到这个工具。

| 字段 | 默认 | 语义 |
|---|---|---|
| `dshHome` | `$DSH_HOME`，否则 `~/.dsh` | 角色目录所依据的 harness home |
| `rolesDir` | `$DSH_HOME/agents` | 你的角色目录：植入目标，也是覆盖根 |
| `seedRolesDir` | `true` | 把内置角色列表写进 `rolesDir`，未改动的跟着包更新 |
| `watchRolesDir` | `true` | `rolesDir` 有文件变动时重新加载角色列表 |
| `commands` | `true` | 每个角色一条 `/<id>` 斜杠指令 |
| `commandPrefix` | （空） | 放在每个指令名前面的文字 |
| `settingsPage` | `true` | 挂载设置 API 与设置页 |
| `provider` | `spawn` | `ctx.subagents` 的 provider 名 |
| `toolName` | `delegate` | 面向模型的工具名 |
| `backgroundMode` | `continuable` | `continuable` 返回 durable child id；`one-shot` 返回 job id |
| `enableRunInBackground` | `true` | 是否暴露 `run_in_background` |
| `maxDepth` | `2` | 被启动 child 的委派深度上限 |
| `defaultRoute` | （空） | 角色没写 `route:` 时使用 |
| `routes` | `{}` | 别名表：`deep: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-flash }` 后角色可写 `route: deep` |

`route:` 依序查：row 的 `routes` 别名表；这个 session 的 `subagent-model-selection` 允许清单（你在 dsh 设置里勾的模型）；已注册 provider 的模型目录；角色文件行内的 `model: { provider, model }`。目录那一步让没有设置界面的 headless profile 也能解析。允许清单开着时它也为角色的路线把关：已注册但不在清单里的模型会得到明确错误，不会偷偷跑。

哪里都没指名路线时，child 沿用调用者的 provider 与 model，结果会注明；插件从不自己从允许清单挑。同一个模型 id 注册在两个 provider 底下时必须写成 `provider/model`。

effort 会夹到该路线声明的层级上，同距离取较高：`deepseek-flash` 提供 `off`／`low`／`high`／`max`，所以 `medium` 变成 `high`、`xhigh` 变成 `max`。内置角色一律写 `high`。发生替换时会在委派结果里注明。
委派请求会指名一个让 child 挂载的 Agent Preset，child 的 persona 与工具完全由那个 preset 决定。某个角色第一次被调用时，插件会针对“这个角色＋调用者的 preset”注册一个 preset：

- **id** 是 `roles-zeta/<角色>@<父 preset>`，例如 `roles-zeta/reviewer@standard`，名称为 `Role: reviewer (standard)`。
- **row** 复制自父 preset 自己的插件 row。`@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona` row 的 `prefix` 换成角色正文，suffix 与其他设置保留；父 preset 没有 persona row 时会补一条。
- **工具插件以插件 row 为单位筛选，不是以工具为单位。** dsh 没有记录哪个插件注册了哪个工具，所以插件内置一张表，列出内置工具插件与各自注册的名称（`dsh-tool-fs`：`read`、`write`、`edit`、`read_image`；`dsh-tool-fs-search`：`glob`、`grep`；其余类推）。有 `allow` 时，只要某个工具插件注册了至少一个允许的名称就保留。没有 `allow` 时全部保留，但注册委派工具（`subagent`、`subagent_fork`、`workflow`、`ralph`）的插件会去掉，除非 `delegation: true`。`allow: []` 不保留任何工具插件。
- **表里没有的 row**（第三方插件，或 `dsh-skill-filesystem`、compaction 这类基础设施）原样保留，因为其他 row 可能依赖它们。一个 group 的 row 全被去掉时，整个 group 也去掉。
- **逐工具遮罩**：child 创建时，再在它自己的 scope 上套一层 `tools.restrict()`。有 `allow` 的 child 只看得到清单里的名称；没有 `allow` 也没设 `delegation: true` 的，会去掉 `delegate`、`subagent`、`subagent_fork`、`workflow`、`ralph`。保留插件的同组工具，以及不属于任何 preset 的 host plane 工具，也一并涵盖。
只要角色文件与父 preset 没变，preset 就会重复使用；两者任一改动，下次调用时会注册新的。角色 child 再委派时，复制的是最初的父 preset，所以 persona 不会叠加。日志会写出每个角色 preset 去掉了哪些 row。

每个 session 一份工具 schema：描述里每个角色一行，加上允许的路线；参数是 `role`、`description`、`prompt`、可选的 `route` 别名、session 开启模型选择时的 `provider`／`model`，以及 `run_in_background`。一次调用会解析角色、预检路线、注册或沿用该角色的 preset，然后在它上面启动一个 child。前台调用返回 child 的最终文本；continuable 后台调用返回 `started subagent <id>`，再由 runtime 的通知结算。

- **preset 仍以整个插件加载，多出的工具由遮罩藏起来。** 只允许 `read` 的 reviewer，保留下来的 `dsh-tool-fs` row 仍会挂上 `write`、`edit`、`read_image`；host plane 的工具（`delegate`、`working_directory`、MCP resource 工具、每个已连接 MCP server 的 `mcp__*` 工具）也仍存在于 preset 之外。两者都到不了 child：逐工具遮罩会藏起 `allow` 没给的每个名称，没有 `allow` 的角色则会失去 `delegate` 与委派工具，除非设了 `delegation: true`。遮罩在 child 创建当下计算，所以之后才注册的允许工具（例如晚一点才连上的 MCP server）对该 child 仍是隐藏的；child 在自己 scope 注册的工具（它的结构化输出工具）则永远不会被遮罩。
- **角色 preset 会和内置 preset 并列。** 它们是普通的 Agent Preset，所以 Web 的 preset 菜单会把它们列在 `standard`、`cordis` 等之后。
- **host 重启后恢复后台 child，需要先有它的 preset。** 角色 preset 是第一次使用时才注册。host 重启前启动的角色 child，在同一个角色从同一个父 preset 再委派一次之前，向它发消息会得到 unknown preset 错误。
- **工具对照表按 dsh 0.2.1-rc.2 建立。** 表里没列的工具插件会整个保留；之后的 dsh 版本若改了工具名，要等表更新才认得。
- **角色改变不了工作区指示链。** 每个 child 与父加载同一条 `AGENTS.md`／`CLAUDE.md` 链。
- **斜杠指令是请求，不是保证。** 委派由模型执行，对话记录会显示它有没有做。
- **设置页改的是文件，不是 session。** 已启动的 child 不受之后的修改影响；下一次启动才读新文件。
- **没有 per-role 记忆。**
